stem: In acute otitis externa, which feature is a late sign?

options.text: Tenderness of the external auditory meatus skin
A draining node on the mastoid tip

explanation: Decreased hearing is a late sign of acute otitis externa.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because tragal tenderness is a common feature of otitis externa, not the late sign described here.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because tenderness of the external auditory meatus is a feature of otitis externa, not the late sign described here.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a draining node on the mastoid tip is not the late sign identified for acute otitis externa.
optionExplanations.D: Correct because decreased hearing is specifically described as a late sign in acute otitis externa.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because otalgia is a typical symptom of otitis externa, but it is not the late sign described here.
